title: Missed Your ITR? Belated and Revised Return Deadline 31 December 2026
excerpt: Missed the ITR due date for FY 2025-26 or made a mistake? Learn the 31 December 2026 deadline, late fees, the new revised-return window to 31 March 2027, and what you lose by filing late.
body:
If you have not yet filed your income tax return for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), you still have time – but not much. The last date for a belated return is **31 December 2026**. The same date matters if you filed your return but spotted a mistake. Here is what you need to know, what it costs, and what you lose by filing late.

## Which deadlines have passed

For income earned in FY 2025-26, the original due dates were:

- **31 July 2026** – ITR-1 and ITR-2 (most salaried people and those with capital gains)
- **31 August 2026** – ITR-3 and ITR-4 for business and professional income without a tax audit
- Later dates for tax audit and transfer pricing cases

If you missed your due date, the return you file now is a **belated return** under section 139(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Returns for FY 2025-26 are still filed under the old Act, even though the Income-tax Act, 2025 has applied from 1 April 2026.

## Belated return: last date and cost

A belated return for FY 2025-26 can be filed **on or before 31 December 2026**, or before the assessment is completed, whichever is earlier.

The cost of filing late:

- **Late fee under section 234F:** ₹5,000, or ₹1,000 if your total income is up to ₹5 lakh
- **Interest under section 234A:** 1% per month on any tax still unpaid, counted from the original due date
- Interest under sections 234B and 234C may also apply if advance tax was short

Pay the tax, interest and late fee through the e-pay tax facility before you submit the return.

## What you lose by filing late

A late fee is not the only price. A belated return also has these limits:

- **Losses:** business losses and capital losses cannot be carried forward to future years if the return is filed after the due date. House property loss and unabsorbed depreciation can still be carried forward.
- **Tax regime choice:** the new tax regime is the default. To choose the old regime, the return (and Form 10-IEA for business or professional income) generally had to be filed by the original due date. A belated return will usually be processed under the new regime, so you may lose deductions such as 80C, 80D and home loan interest.
- **Refunds:** you can still claim a refund in a belated return, but it may take longer and you may get less interest on it.

## Revised return: fixing a mistake

If you filed your return – on time or late – and later find an error, such as missed income, a wrong deduction or a wrong bank account, you can file a **revised return** under section 139(5). A belated return can also be revised.

The time limit has changed from this year. After the Budget 2026 amendment, a revised return for FY 2025-26 can be filed up to **31 March 2027** (or before assessment is completed, if earlier):

- **Revised by 31 December 2026:** no fee
- **Revised from 1 January to 31 March 2027:** a fee under section 234I of ₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh, and ₹5,000 above ₹5 lakh

So if you already know your return has an error, revise it before 31 December 2026 to avoid the fee. If you filed a belated return and revise it after 31 December, you may end up paying both the 234F and 234I fees.

## Missed 31 December? The updated return

If both dates pass, you can still file an **updated return (ITR-U)** under section 139(8A). It can be filed within 48 months from the end of the assessment year, but it comes with a price:

- Additional tax of 25% to 70% of the tax and interest due, depending on how late you file
- It cannot be used to claim a refund, increase a loss or reduce your tax
- Only one updated return can be filed for a year

ITR-U is a way to correct missed income and avoid bigger trouble later. It is far cheaper to file a belated or revised return before 31 December.

## Quick checklist before 31 December 2026

- Download your **AIS and Form 26AS** and match them with your Form 16, bank interest and capital gains statements
- Check TDS credit, especially on rent, fixed deposits and professional fees
- Pay any balance tax with interest and the late fee
- Choose the correct ITR form and verify the return within 30 days of filing (Aadhaar OTP or net banking is quickest)
- If you already filed, check the processing intimation under section 143(1) and revise now if anything is wrong
